candidates.teaser: For 84 years, this machine beat Napoleon and Benjamin Franklin at chess — and nobody figured out its secret.
candidates.video_title: The Machine That Beat Napoleon at Chess
candidates.video_description: The Turk was an 18th-century chess-playing automaton that defeated some of history's greatest minds. It toured Europe and America for 84 years before its secret was finally revealed. The truth was far stranger than any mechanism.
candidates.script: A wooden machine beat Napoleon Bonaparte at chess in 1809 — and he had no idea he was being deceived. The Turk toured Europe for 84 years, defeating kings, presidents, and geniuses. It appeared to think, to calculate, to win on pure logic. Engineers tore it apart looking for hidden gears. They found none. The secret? A chess grandmaster folded inside, shifting magnets from below. Every match was a magic trick nobody solved for nearly a century. So — when does a brilliant illusion become a lie?

candidates.topic: Pando — The Single Organism That Weighs 6 Million Kilograms
candidates.teaser: There's a single living thing in Utah that has been alive for 80,000 years — and you'd never know it by looking at it.
candidates.video_title: This Forest Is Actually One Single Creature
candidates.video_description: Pando is a colony of quaking aspen trees in Utah that share a single root system, making them one organism. It weighs over 6 million kilograms and may be 80,000 years old. It is the heaviest known living thing on Earth — and it's dying.
candidates.script: What looks like an entire forest in Utah is actually one single living creature. Every tree you see — all 47,000 of them — shares the same root system, the same DNA, the same organism. It's called Pando. It weighs over 6 million kilograms, making it the heaviest thing alive on Earth, and it may have existed for 80,000 years. It survived ice ages, droughts, and mass extinctions. But right now, in 2024, it's shrinking — and scientists aren't sure they can stop it.

candidates.topic: The Last Breath Statistic — Caesar's Final Exhale
candidates.teaser: Every time you breathe in, statistically you're inhaling molecules from some of history's most famous last moments.
candidates.video_title: You're Breathing Julius Caesar's Last Breath
candidates.video_description: Atmospheric science reveals that the molecules exhaled by Julius Caesar at his death in 44 BC have had over 2,000 years to spread evenly across Earth's atmosphere. Each breath you take statistically contains about one of those exact molecules. The math is real.
candidates.script: Right now, breathing normally, you are almost certainly inhaling a molecule that Julius Caesar exhaled as he died. This isn't poetry — it's atmospheric chemistry. Caesar was assassinated in 44 BC. His last breath contained roughly 25 sextillion molecules. In 2,000 years, they've dispersed so evenly across Earth's atmosphere that statistically, every single breath you take contains at least one of them. The same applies to Cleopatra. To Shakespeare. To every human who ever lived. What does that do to your idea of death?

candidates.topic: Phantom Limb Pain — The Brain Invents Suffering
candidates.teaser: Doctors found a way to cure pain in a limb that doesn't exist — using nothing but a mirror.
candidates.video_title: The Mirror That Cures Pain in a Missing Arm
candidates.video_description: Phantom limb pain affects up to 80% of amputees — the brain continues sending pain signals to a limb that no longer exists. Neuroscientist V.S. Ramachandran discovered in 1993 that a simple mirror box could trick the brain into releasing that pain instantly. It revealed how completely the brain constructs our reality.
candidates.script: Soldiers who lose an arm in combat often scream from pain — in the arm that's gone. The brain keeps firing signals to a limb that no longer exists, and it hurts just as much as a real injury. In 1993, neuroscientist V.S. Ramachandran cured this with a cardboard box and a mirror. The patient watched their reflection move a phantom hand — and the pain vanished. The brain believed the reflection was real. That means your pain, your body, your reality — all of it is something your brain is actively constructing right now.

candidates.teaser: One night in 1986, a lake in Africa silently killed 1,700 people in under an hour — without a single explosion or wave.
candidates.video_title: The Lake That Silently Killed 1,700 People
candidates.video_description: On August 21, 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon released a massive burst of carbon dioxide from its depths, suffocating 1,700 people and 3,500 livestock within a 25-kilometer radius — all while the lake itself remained completely calm. It is one of the deadliest natural disasters caused by a body of water in recorded history.
candidates.script: On August 21st, 1986, a lake in Cameroon murdered 1,700 people without making a single sound. No tsunami, no earthquake, no warning. Lake Nyos simply exhaled. A pocket of carbon dioxide had been building for centuries in the deep water. That night it released all at once — a silent, invisible cloud that rolled across 25 kilometers of villages at highway speed, replacing every molecule of oxygen. People were found dead mid-stride. Animals collapsed in fields. The lake turned blood red. Scientists say several other lakes worldwide are doing the same thing right now.
